text:
X-rays are classified as hard and soft based on the following characters:
(A). Density
(B). Current
(C). Penetrating power
(D). Wavelength
(E). Frequency
explanation: Hard and soft X-rays are differentiated on the basis of their penetrating power — hard X-rays are highly penetrating (short wavelength/high energy) while soft X-rays are weakly penetrating.

text:
In ruminants, acetonemia is primarily seen due to:
(A). Disorders of carbohydrate metabolism
(B). Disorders of fat metabolism
(C). Disorders of protein metabolism
(D). Disorder of B-complex vitamins
(E). Deficiency of calcium and magnesium
explanation: Bovine ketosis (acetonemia) results from negative energy balance, i.e., a disturbance of carbohydrate metabolism, leading to excessive mobilisation of body fat and ketone body formation.

text:
Staphylococcus pseudointermedius can be identified on the basis of following characters:
(A). Coagulase negative
(B). Susceptible to polymyxin B
(C). V P test positive
(D). β-galactosidase positive
explanation: S. pseudintermedius (Staphylococcus intermedius group) is coagulase-positive and VP-negative, but is characteristically susceptible to polymyxin B and β-galactosidase positive — features used to differentiate it from S. aureus.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Sabin-Feldman dye test
(B). Knott's Technique
(C). Capillary tube agglutination
(D). Animal inoculation test
List II:
(I). Trypanosomiasis
(II). Anaplasmosis
(III). Filariosis
(IV). Toxoplasmosis
options: A – II, B – III, C – IV, D – I
A – IV, B – II, C – I, D – III
A – IV, B – III, C – II, D – I
A – III, B – II, C – I, D – IV
explanation: Sabin-Feldman dye test = Toxoplasmosis; Knott's technique concentrates and detects microfilariae = Filariosis; Capillary/card agglutination test = Anaplasmosis; Animal (rodent) inoculation test = Trypanosomiasis.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Epiplocele
(B). Vesicocele
(C). Hysterocele
(D). Omphalocele
List II:
(I). Uterus
(II). Omentum
(III). Umbilical region
(IV). Bladder
options: A – II, B – IV, C – III, D – I
A – II, B – III, C – I, D – IV
A – I, B – II, C – III, D – IV
A – II, B – IV, C – I, D – III
explanation: Epiplocele = hernia of omentum; Vesicocele = hernia of urinary bladder; Hysterocele = hernia of the uterus; Omphalocele = hernia at the umbilical region.

text: What percentage of the medullar cavity of the fractured bone should the narrowest point of the intramedullary pin fill?
explanation: An intramedullary pin should occupy about 65–75% of the medullary canal diameter at its narrowest point for adequate stability without excess cortical weakening.

text: Insecticide resistance can be avoided by:
options: Continuous use of same insecticide for a long time
Use of higher doses of insecticides
explanation: Rotating insecticide classes/mode-of-action groups (not just brand names) prevents selection pressure for resistance genes within a single target pathway.

text: On daily basis, which immunoglobulin is produced in maximum amount?
explanation: Although serum IgG concentration is highest, the mucosal immune system (gut, respiratory, mammary) produces more IgA per day than any other immunoglobulin class.

text: In dogs, weighing 10 Kg BW, functional concentration of 30-40% oxygen can be achieved through an in venous catheter positioned transtracheally if the flow rate of oxygen is:
explanation: Transtracheal oxygen delivery bypasses upper airway dead space, so a low flow of about 1–2 L/min is sufficient to achieve 30–40% inspired oxygen in a small dog.

text: Sertoli Cell Tumour is most likely to occur:
options: In ovary of 8-12 year old bitch
In retained testicle of 7 year old dog
In distal limb of 6 month old dog
explanation: Sertoli cell tumours arise from testicular sex-cord stroma and are strongly associated with cryptorchid (retained) testes in older dogs.

text:
In dogs, irregular pulse in femoral artery is indicative of:
(A). Myocardial damage
(B). Nephritis
(C). Hepatitis
(D). Brain disease
(E). Pancreatitis
explanation: An irregular femoral pulse (pulse deficit) reflects cardiac arrhythmia, which results from myocardial damage/disease.

text: Phonendoscope was invented by:
explanation: The phonendoscope, an enhanced stethoscope, was invented by Bazzi and improved/popularised by Bianchi.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): Cystitis is usually NOT associated with a bacterial infection.
Statement (II): It is clinically characterized by pollakiuria, dysuria, and hematuria.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
explanation: Cystitis is, in fact, most often associated with bacterial (ascending) infection, so Statement I is false; the classic clinical signs are pollakiuria, dysuria and haematuria, so Statement II is true.

text: Larval stage of which parasite is found in the peritoneal cavity of sheep?
explanation: The larval (metacestode) stage of Taenia hydatigena, called Cysticercus tenuicollis, is commonly found in the peritoneal cavity/liver of sheep.

text: Ciprofloxacin inhibits the following enzyme in eukaryotic cells:
explanation: While fluoroquinolones primarily target bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, their off-target action in eukaryotic cells is on topoisomerase II.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): In cattle, ultrasonography is superior for visualization of small volumes of pleural fluid.
Statement (II): The pleural fluid can be detected by auscultation and acoustic percussion.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
explanation: Ultrasonography detects even small amounts of pleural fluid better than any other method, and larger accumulations are also classically detectable clinically by dull percussion and muffled auscultation — both statements are true.

text: Enzootic abortion of ewes (EAE) is caused by:
explanation: Enzootic abortion of ewes is caused by Chlamydophila (Chlamydia) abortus, producing characteristic placentitis and late-term abortion.

text:
In which disease condition, recurrent bloat is seen:
(A). Diaphragmatic hernia
(B). Legume bloat
(C). Enteritis
(D). Vagal indigestion
(E). Rhinitis
explanation: Diaphragmatic hernia and vagal indigestion both interfere with the normal eructation reflex/forestomach motility, producing recurrent bloat.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): Trichophyton mentagrophyte perforates hair shaft and produces wedge-shaped areas in hair perforation test.
Statement (II): Hair perforation test is used to distinguish Trichophyton mentagrophyte from Trichophyton rubrum.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
explanation: T. mentagrophytes gives a positive (wedge-shaped perforation) in vitro hair perforation test, while T. rubrum is negative — this is exactly why the test is used to differentiate the two dermatophytes.

text: Holometabola belongs to which group of insects?
explanation: Fleas (Siphonaptera) undergo complete (holometabolous) metamorphosis with egg-larva-pupa-adult stages, unlike lice and bugs which are hemimetabolous, and ticks which are not insects at all.

text: Ingluviotomy in chicken is indicated for the:
explanation: Ingluviotomy is surgical incision of the ingluvies (crop), performed to relieve crop impaction.

text: White heifers' disease is associated with:
explanation: White heifer disease is a congenital anomaly of the Müllerian duct system in white Shorthorn cattle, resulting in segmental genital tract aplasia and a functional uterus unicornis.

text: α – Fetoprotein causes:
options: De-feminization of surge center of hypothalamus
Differentiation of male and female sex
explanation: α-Fetoprotein binds circulating oestrogen in the fetal/neonatal female, protecting the brain from masculinising oestrogen exposure and thereby permitting normal sexual differentiation.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): Potato soup coloured discharge in cattle is seen in Trichomonas infection.
Statement (II): Pyometra in cattle is caused by Trichomonas infection.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
explanation: Tritrichomonas foetus infection classically produces a thick, purulent, 'potato-soup'-like uterine discharge and is a recognised cause of bovine pyometra — both statements are true.

text:
In acidic urine, we may observe the following type of crystals during microscopic examination:
(A). Uric Acid
(B). Triple phosphate
(C). Calcium oxalate
(D). Hippuric acid
(E). Amorphous phosphate
explanation: Uric acid, calcium oxalate and hippuric acid crystals form in acidic urine, whereas triple (struvite) phosphate and amorphous phosphate crystallise in alkaline urine.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Hydroallantois
(B). Mummified fetus
(C). ECG (equine chorionic gonadotropin)
(D). Pseudo pregnancy in bitch
List II:
(I). Cabergoline
(II). Bloated bull frog
(III). Persistent corpus luteum
(IV). Placental hormone
options: A – II, B – III, C – IV, D – I
A – III, B – IV, C – I, D - II
A – IV, B – I, C – II, D – III
A – I, B – II, C – III, D – IV
explanation: ECG (eCG/PMSG) is a placental gonadotropic hormone; mummified fetus results from a persistent corpus luteum maintaining pregnancy hormonally; cabergoline (a dopamine agonist/anti-prolactin) is used to manage pseudopregnancy in the bitch; hydroallantois pairs with the remaining option by elimination.

text:
In cirrhosis of liver, following post-mortem findings are recorded:
(A). Presence of normal architecture
(B). Fatty infiltration
(C). Degeneration of hepatocytes
(D). Loss of intracellular connective tissue matrix
(E). Atrophy of the liver
explanation: Cirrhosis shows hepatocyte degeneration and, in advanced stages, a small/atrophic, nodular liver; normal architecture is lost (not preserved) and fibrous connective tissue increases rather than being lost.

text: Obtectate type of pupa is characteristic of:
explanation: Unlike most higher Diptera (which form a coarctate puparium, e.g. Calliphoridae) or exarate pupae (e.g. Tabanidae), Psychodidae (moth flies) are unusual among flies in having an obtect pupa.

text: Which among the following acts as entry receptor of Rabies virus?
explanation: The nicotinic acetylcholine receptor is one of the classically described cellular entry receptors used by the rabies virus at the neuromuscular junction.

text:
Which of the following is used as antidote for cyanide poisoning in bovines?
(A). Sodium EDTA
(B). Sodium nitrite
(C). Sodium thiosulphate
(D). Dimercaprol
(E). BAL
explanation: Sodium nitrite (generates methaemoglobin to bind cyanide) followed by sodium thiosulphate (provides sulphur for rhodanese to form thiocyanate) is the classic two-step antidote regimen for cyanide poisoning.

text: What is the appropriate time for injection of Vitamin D3 to prevent occurrence of Milk fever?
explanation: Vitamin D3 injections are recommended about one week before expected calving; given earlier, its hypercalcaemic effect wanes before parturition.

text:
The primary causes of non-inflammatory edema include:
(A). Increased intravascular hydrostatic pressure
(B). Increased vascular permeability
(C). Increased colloid osmotic pressure
(D). Lymphatic obstruction
(E). Electrocution
explanation: Non-inflammatory (transudative) oedema arises from increased hydrostatic pressure or lymphatic obstruction/decreased oncotic pressure, whereas increased vascular permeability is the hallmark of inflammatory oedema.

text: On post-mortem examination, cloudiness of air sac membrane with pericarditis and fibrinous perihepatitis are noticed in which disease?
explanation: Airsacculitis with fibrinous pericarditis and perihepatitis is the classic triad of avian colibacillosis (colisepticaemia).

text: During rumenotomy the rumen is fixed to the skin by using:
explanation: Weingarth's ring/frame is the instrument classically used to fix the rumen wall to the skin incision during rumenotomy.

text:
Which of the following enzyme hydrolyses the acetylcholine?
(A). Acetylcholine transferase
(B). Acetylcholine esterase
(C). Acetylcholine dehydrogenase
(D). Sorbitol dehydrogenase
(E). Monoamine oxidase
explanation: Acetylcholinesterase hydrolyses acetylcholine into choline and acetate, terminating cholinergic neurotransmission.

text: Spinnbarkeit test of the cervical mucus is used to measure:
explanation: Spinnbarkeit refers to the stretchability/elasticity of oestrogen-dominated cervical mucus, tested by drawing it into a thread.

text: A new class of anthelmintic monepantel is member of:
explanation: Monepantel belongs to the amino-acetonitrile derivative (AAD) class of anthelmintics, acting on nematode-specific acetylcholine receptor subunits.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): Kumri is a condition caused by Setaria digitata in cattle.
Statement (II): The pathogenic effects in cattle are mainly due to erratic migration of mature worms in the Central Nervous System.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
explanation: Cattle are the normal (definitive) host of Setaria digitata and remain asymptomatic; Kumri (lumbar paralysis) occurs in aberrant hosts such as horses, sheep and goats, so Statement I is false. The CNS damage in aberrant hosts is indeed due to erratic larval/worm migration, so Statement II is true.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Fetal dystocia
(B). Isthmo-ampullary junction of fallopian tube
(C). Negative energy balance
(D). French mini straw
List II:
(I). 0.25 ml
(II). Infertility
(III). Common in polytocous species
(IV). Fertilization
options: A – I, B – III, C – IV, D – II
A – IV, B – I, C – III, D – II
A – I, B – II, C – IV, D – III
A – III, B – IV, C – II, D – I
explanation: French mini straws hold 0.25 ml of semen; negative energy balance is a major cause of infertility in dairy cattle; fertilisation occurs at the isthmo-ampullary junction; fetal-related dystocia (malpresentation) is comparatively more common in polytocous species.

text: Salbutamol causes bronchodilation by its action on:
explanation: Salbutamol is a selective β2-adrenergic agonist, causing bronchial smooth muscle relaxation and bronchodilation.

text: The second messenger cAMP is inactivated by:
explanation: Phosphodiesterase hydrolyses cAMP to inactive 5'-AMP, terminating its second-messenger signal; adenylyl cyclase, in contrast, synthesises cAMP.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Increased prolactin
(B). Cabergoline
(C). Mifepristone
(D). Prostaglandin F2α
List II:
(I). Termination of pregnancy in bitches without side effects
(II). Treatment of pyometra in bitches
(III). Induction of estrus in bitches
(IV). Pseudopregnancy
options: A – II, B – IV, C – III, D – I
A – III, B – II, C – IV, D – I
A – IV, B – III, C – I, D – II
A – IV, B – I, C – II, D – III
explanation: Increased prolactin causes pseudopregnancy; cabergoline (a dopamine agonist/prolactin inhibitor) is used to terminate pregnancy with minimal side effects; the antiprogestin mifepristone is used to treat pyometra; prostaglandin F2α is used to induce/synchronize estrus.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Husk or Hoose
(B). Verminous endarteritis
(C). Anaemia in pups
(D). Visceral larva migrans
List II:
(I). Strongylus vulgaris
(II). Ancylostoma caninum
(III). Dictyocaulus viviparous
(IV). Toxocara canis
options: A – III, B – I, C – IV, D – II
A – II, B – III, C – I, D – IV
A – II, B – IV, C – III, D – I
A – III, B – I, C – II, D – IV
explanation: Husk/hoose (lungworm disease) is caused by Dictyocaulus viviparus; verminous endarteritis in horses by Strongylus vulgaris; anaemia in pups by the hookworm Ancylostoma caninum; visceral larva migrans by Toxocara canis.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Dacrocystorhinography
(B). Intravenous pyelography
(C). EEG
(D). Sialography
List II:
(I). Encephalomalacia
(II). Salivary gland
(III). Kidney and ureters
(IV). Urinary bladder
options: A – II, B – III, C – IV, D – I
A – IV, B – III, C – I, D – II
A – I, B – II, C – III, D – IV
A – III, B – IV, C – II, D – I
explanation: Sialography images the salivary glands; intravenous pyelography images the kidneys and ureters; EEG helps assess brain lesions such as encephalomalacia; dacryocystorhinography pairs with the remaining option by elimination.

text:
Increase in progesterone level is required for ovulation in which species?
(A). Mare
(B). Bitch
(C). Cattle
(D). Camel
(E). Goat
explanation: In the bitch, pre-ovulatory luteinisation of follicles causes progesterone to begin rising before ovulation itself occurs — a feature unique among domestic species.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): Macrocyclic lactone (ivermectin) is not effective against trematodes and cestodes.
Statement (II): The inhibitory neurotransmitter present in trematodes and cestodes is glycine.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
explanation: Ivermectin indeed has no efficacy against trematodes/cestodes because they lack the glutamate-gated chloride channels ivermectin targets — Statement I is true. Statement II's claim about glycine being their inhibitory neurotransmitter is not the accepted basis for this resistance, so it is false.

text: Which of the following materials is used as an antigen in Casoni's test?
explanation: Casoni's intradermal test uses sterile hydatid cyst fluid as antigen to detect hypersensitivity in hydatidosis (Echinococcus) infection.

text:
Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy helps in the diagnosis of:
(A). Hypertrophic gastritis
(B). Abnormal motility
(C). Esophagitis
(D). Enteritis
(E). Colitis
explanation: Upper GI endoscopy visualises the oesophagus and stomach, allowing diagnosis of oesophagitis and gastritis; enteritis and colitis are lower GI conditions not assessed by upper endoscopy.

text: Omeprazole produces antacid action by inhibiting:
explanation: Omeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor that irreversibly blocks the gastric parietal cell H+/K+ ATPase, reducing acid secretion.

text:
Brucella abortus Indian Biovar(s) has following characteristics:
(A). It is modified Z N staining negative
(B). It is grown under 5 – 10% CO2 concentration
(C). It is urease positive
(D). It is non-H2S producer
(E). Thayer Martin medium does not show its growth
explanation: Brucella abortus (including the Indian biovar) is urease-positive and, being a capnophilic biovar, requires increased (5–10%) CO2 for growth.

text: Multi fragmented fracture fixation in dogs with dynamic compression plate is called:
explanation: When a plate spans multiple (comminuted) fragments and supports/prevents their collapse under load rather than compressing bone ends together, the technique is termed buttress plating.

text: The early embryo in the uterus is nourished by:
explanation: Before placental attachment is established, the early embryo/conceptus is nourished by histotrophic nutrition — secretions ('uterine milk') from the endometrial glands.

text: The wound is known as infected if the bacterial count exceeds:
options: 10^5 number of bacteria per gram of tissue
10^6 number of bacteria per gram of tissue
10^2 number of bacteria per gram of tissue
10^8 number of bacteria per gram of tissue
explanation: A tissue bacterial load exceeding 10^5 organisms per gram is the standard surgical threshold defining a wound as infected.

text: Possession of F – 18 Fimbriae and production of Stx2e toxin and haemolysin is related to which pathotype of Escherichia coli?
explanation: F18-fimbriated E. coli producing Shiga toxin 2e (edema disease E. coli) belongs to the Shiga toxin-producing (Shigatoxigenic) pathotype.

text:
Ovulation during primary oocyte stage occurs in which of the following species?
(A). Cow
(B). Buffalo
(C). Bitch
(D). Mare
(E). Goat
explanation: Uniquely among domestic species, the bitch ovulates a primary oocyte, which completes maturation to the secondary oocyte stage within the oviduct 2–3 days after ovulation.

text: Split estrus is seen in:
explanation: Young bitches occasionally show 'split estrus' — proestrus signs that regress and then recur before true behavioural estrus and ovulation occur.

text: A setting in an X-ray machine indicates:
explanation: The milliampere (mA) setting of an X-ray machine controls the tube (tubular) current, i.e., the flow of electrons across the tube.

text: Fetal sex determination using ultrasonography can be done in cattle between:
explanation: In cattle, ultrasonographic fetal sexing (based on genital tubercle location) is most reliably done between about 60 and 80 days of gestation.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Stiff lamb disease
(B). Azoturia
(C). Trichinella spiralis
(D). Black quarter
List II:
(I). Myoglobinuria
(II). Parasitic myositis
(III). White muscle disease
(IV). Gangrenous myositis
options: A – III, B – I, C – II, D – IV
A – I, B – II, C – IV, D - III
A – II, B – IV, C – III, D - I
A – IV, B – III, C – I, D – II
explanation: Stiff lamb disease is another name for nutritional white muscle disease; azoturia (exertional rhabdomyolysis) causes myoglobinuria; Trichinella spiralis causes parasitic myositis; blackleg (black quarter) causes gangrenous myositis.

text: Nerve block for enucleation of eye ball in cattle is:
explanation: A retrobulbar nerve block anaesthetises the eye and surrounding structures, commonly used for enucleation in cattle.

text: Milliamperage (mA) setting in an X – ray machine decides the:
explanation: mA determines the number of electrons (and hence X-ray photons) produced, i.e., the quantity of X-rays; kVp determines their quality/penetrating power.

text:
To assess the function of liver, we can use following tests in dog:
(A). BSP clearance test
(B). Estimation of LDH enzyme
(C). Estimation of bilirubin
(D). Trypsin test
(E). Test for malabsorption of intestine
explanation: BSP (bromosulphthalein) clearance and serum bilirubin estimation are classic, specific tests of hepatic function in dogs.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): Trichomoniasis in bulls can be diagnosed by examination of serum using MAT test.
Statement (II): Brucellosis in cattle causes disease of the placenta.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
explanation: Bovine trichomoniasis is diagnosed from preputial washings/culture, not by a serum MAT test (which is used for toxoplasmosis) — Statement I is false. Brucellosis characteristically causes placentitis, so Statement II is true.

text: Which of the following fungi is used for biological control of nematodes?
explanation: Duddingtonia flagrans is a nematode-trapping (nematophagous) fungus widely used for the biological control of gastrointestinal nematodes on pasture.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Copper
(B). Arsenic
(C). Selenium
(D). Mercury
List II:
(I). Rice water diarrhoea
(II). Blind staggers
(III). Damage to fetal nervous system
(IV). Port wine coloured urine
options: A – I, B – II, C – III, D – IV
A – II, B – III, C – IV, D - I
A – III, B – IV, C – I, D - II
A – IV, B – I, C – II, D – III
explanation: Copper toxicosis causes intravascular haemolysis and port-wine coloured urine; arsenic poisoning causes rice-water diarrhoea; selenium toxicosis causes blind staggers; mercury is teratogenic, damaging the fetal nervous system.

text: Which one of the following is an INCORRECT pair?
explanation: Gid (coenurosis) is caused by Coenurus cerebralis (Taenia multiceps), not Cysticercus tenuicollis, making this the incorrect pair.

text: The site of incision for pericardiotomy in bovines is:
options: Along the fifth rib on the left side
Along the sixth rib on the right side
Along the fifth rib on the right side
explanation: Pericardiotomy in cattle is classically performed through an incision along the left fifth intercostal space/rib.

text: Reconstructive surgery is surgery done for:
options: Removal of root cause of disease
explanation: Reconstructive surgery aims to correct deformities and restore form/function, distinguishing it from curative or diagnostic procedures.

text: Abnormal gastric distension causes dog sitting posture which is common among:
explanation: Gastric distension/colic in horses classically produces a characteristic 'dog-sitting' posture as the animal attempts to relieve abdominal pain.

text: Which type of stomatitis is produced in case of actinomycosis?
explanation: Actinomycosis ('lumpy jaw') produces chronic pyogranulomatous lesions with marked bony proliferation and sclerosis, giving a sclerosing character to the lesion.

text: β- Carotene is a rich source of:
explanation: β-Carotene is a provitamin that is enzymatically cleaved in the body to form Vitamin A (retinol).

text:
The mode of infection of Toxocara canis is:
(A). Ingestion of infective eggs
(B). Direct skin penetration
(C). Aerosol route of transmission
(D). Lactogenic route of infection
(E). Ingestion of infected paratenic host
explanation: Toxocara canis is transmitted mainly by ingestion of infective eggs, the lactogenic (transmammary) route, and ingestion of infected paratenic hosts (e.g. rodents); aerosol transmission does not occur.

text:
Which of the following bacteria produce endospores?
(A). Actinomyces spp.
(B). Bacillus anthracis
(C). Nocardia spp.
(D). Clostridium spp.
(E). Dermatophillus spp.
explanation: Only Bacillus and Clostridium species among bacteria form true endospores; Actinomyces, Nocardia and Dermatophilus do not.

text:
The following tests can be applied to determine Minimum Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) values against an isolated bacterium:
(A). Kirby Bauer method
(B). Broth Dilution method
(C). E – test
(D). Miles Mishra Technique
explanation: Broth dilution and the E-test give a quantitative MIC value, whereas the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method is only qualitative, and Miles-Misra is a viable count technique.

text:
The adverse effect of xylazine hydrochloride is reversed with the use of:
(A). Neostigmine
(B). Atropine sulphate
(C). Acetyl choline
(D). Yohimbine hydrochloride
(E). Dopamine
explanation: Yohimbine, an alpha-2 adrenergic antagonist, is the specific reversal agent for xylazine's sedative/adverse effects.

text:
Which of the following phase I enzymes has major contribution in drug metabolism?
(A). CYP2A6
(B). CYP2D6
(C). CYP3A4
(D). CYP2D9
(E). CYP3A9
explanation: CYP3A4 is the most abundant hepatic cytochrome P450 isoform and metabolises the largest proportion of drugs.

text: Signs of neo-natal hypoglycemia in piglets occur when the blood glucose levels falls to about:
explanation: Clinical hypoglycaemia in neonatal piglets is typically seen once blood glucose falls to around 50 mg/dL or below.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Hyperadrenocorticism
(B). Vitamin-E and Selenium
(C). Scabies
(D). Spinal Cord disease
List II:
(I). Obesity
(II). Muscular dystrophy
(III). Postural reactions
(IV). Intense pruritis
options: A – I, B – II, C – IV, D – III
A – II, B – IV, C – III, D – I
A – IV, B – III, C – I, D – II
A – III, B – II, C – IV, D – I
explanation: Hyperadrenocorticism (Cushing's) causes obesity; Vitamin E/Selenium deficiency causes nutritional muscular dystrophy; scabies causes intense pruritis; spinal cord disease is assessed via postural reaction deficits.

text: Which one of the following morphological features is related to Trichuris ovis?
options: Whip like appearance of the parasite
explanation: Trichuris (whipworm) species have a characteristic whip-like body — a long thin anterior end and a thicker posterior end.

text: Colour code of nitrous oxide cylinder in India is:
explanation: In India, nitrous oxide gas cylinders are colour-coded blue.

text: Horn cancer is a malignant tumour of which type of cells?
explanation: Horn cancer in cattle is a squamous cell carcinoma arising from the keratinised epithelium of the horn.

text: Which of the following animals has Type – II Peyer's Patches which are located at random intervals in ileum and jejunum?
explanation: Rabbits characteristically possess multiple, persistent (Type II) Peyer's patches scattered along the jejunum and ileum, in addition to the large ileocaecal sacculus rotundus.

text: What is the range of pH of normal cow milk?
explanation: Fresh normal cow milk has a pH in the slightly acidic range of about 6.6–6.8.

text:
The viruses belonging to family Parvoviridae have the following characters:
(A). Icosahedral symmetry
(B). Enveloped virion
(C). Single stranded RNA
(D). Single stranded DNA
(E). Replication in nucleus of host cell
explanation: Parvoviruses are small, non-enveloped, icosahedral viruses with a single-stranded DNA genome that replicate in the host cell nucleus.

text: Contagious acne (Canadian horse pox) is caused by:
explanation: 'Canadian horsepox'/contagious acne of horses is caused by Corynebacterium pseudotuberculosis (equine biovar), producing folliculitis/pustular skin lesions.

text: Part Film Distance (PFD) in radiography must be:
explanation: The body part being radiographed should be placed in direct contact with the film/cassette (i.e., PFD = 0) to minimise magnification and geometric distortion.

text:
For queen cat, balanced anesthesia involves administration of a sequence of the following drugs:
(A). Ketamine hydrochloride
(B). Atropine Sulphate
(C). Diazepam
(D). Xylazine hydrochloride
explanation: A typical balanced anaesthesia protocol premedicates with atropine, then a sedative (xylazine), then diazepam, followed by the dissociative agent ketamine for induction.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Cysteine Crystals
(B). Struvite Crystals
(C). Gag reflex
(D). Gastrocnemius reflex
List II:
(I). Vagus Nerve
(II). L7 – S1
(III). Alkaline urine
(IV). Acidic Urine
options: A – IV, B – III, C – I, D – II
A – III, B – II, C – I, D – IV
A – II, B – I, C – III, D – IV
A – I, B – II, C – IV, D – III
explanation: Cystine crystals form in acidic urine; struvite (triple phosphate) crystals form in alkaline urine; the gag reflex is mediated via the vagus (and glossopharyngeal) nerve; the gastrocnemius reflex tests the L7–S1 spinal segment.

text:
Atropine sulphate is contraindicated in the patients suffering from:
(A). Heart failure
(B). Dyspnea
(C). Pre-existing tachycardia
(D). Vomition
(E). Enteritis
explanation: Atropine increases heart rate and myocardial oxygen demand, so it is contraindicated in animals with heart failure or pre-existing tachycardia/tachyarrhythmias.

text: Nipah virus belongs to which genus of the family Paramyxoviridae?
explanation: Nipah virus, along with Hendra virus, belongs to the genus Henipavirus within family Paramyxoviridae.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): Male feminizing syndrome in dogs occurs due to Sertoli Cell tumour.
Statement (II): Gynaecomastia in male feminizing syndrome occurs due to tumour of Leydig cell.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
explanation: Male feminizing syndrome and its features including gynaecomastia arise from oestrogen-secreting Sertoli cell tumours, not Leydig cell tumours — Statement II is false.

text: Which among the following is a primary binding/serological test?
explanation: ELISA is a primary binding assay that directly measures antigen-antibody binding via a labelled reagent, unlike agglutination, precipitation and complement fixation, which are secondary tests relying on a visible end reaction.

text:
Specific gravity is the principle involved in the following methods of faecal examination:
(A). Direct smear method
(B). Lanes technique
(C). Agglutination test
(D). Willis technique
(E). Faecal trypsin test
explanation: Willis' flotation technique and Lane's technique both rely on a solution of high specific gravity to float parasite eggs/oocysts above faecal debris.

text: The fracture of proximal end of ulna is known as:
explanation: A fracture of the proximal ulna, typically with radial head luxation, is termed a Monteggia fracture.

text: An example of tendon suture is:
explanation: The Bunnell suture is a classic locking-loop pattern used for tendon repair.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Cubones test
(B). Endometrial cups
(C). Oxytocin
(D). Tocolysis
List II:
(I). Induction of parturition in mare
(II). Prevention of uterine contractions
(III). ECG
(IV). Estrogen
options: A – III, B – IV, C – II, D – I
A – IV, B – I, C – II, D – III
A – II, B – III, C – IV, D – I
A – IV, B – III, C – I, D – II
explanation: The Cuboni test detects oestrogen conjugates in mare urine for pregnancy diagnosis; endometrial cups secrete equine chorionic gonadotropin (eCG); oxytocin is used to induce parturition; tocolysis means preventing/suppressing uterine contractions.

text:
Which of the following are burrowing mites?
(A). Sarcoptes scabiei
(B). Psoroptes ovis
(C). Notoedres cati
(D). Chorioptes bovis
(E). Cnemidocoptes mutans
explanation: Sarcoptes, Notoedres and Cnemidocoptes are burrowing mites that tunnel into the epidermis; Psoroptes and Chorioptes are surface-dwelling, non-burrowing mites.

text: Theiler's disease is the most common cause of acute hepatitis in:
explanation: Theiler's disease (serum hepatitis), often linked to administration of equine biological products, is a major cause of acute hepatic necrosis in horses.

text: Choosing the forelegs in a postural abnormality occurs during fracture of 3rd phalanges in case of:
explanation: Because of the split-claw weight-bearing anatomy in cattle, a fractured third phalanx often results in a characteristic weight-shifting/postural change onto the forelimbs.

text: Which ELISA is used to differentiate between infected and vaccinated animal in Foot and Mouth disease?
explanation: NSP-based ELISA detects antibodies against viral non-structural proteins, which are present only after natural infection (not after vaccination with purified antigen), thereby serving as a DIVA (Differentiating Infected from Vaccinated Animals) test.

text:
Select the correct sequence of Schistosoma nasale life cycle:
(A). Redia
(B). Cercaria
(C). Miracidium
(D). Sporocyst
(E). Metacercaria
explanation: Schistosomes (blood flukes) lack a redia stage and their cercariae directly infect the host without forming metacercariae; the cycle proceeds miracidium → sporocyst → cercaria.

text: Gag reflex test is carried out to test the cranial nerve namely:
explanation: The gag reflex tests the glossopharyngeal (afferent) and vagus (efferent) nerves.

text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): The general principles of mastitis control is unsuccessful for the control of coliform mastitis.
Statement (II): Because infection of the mammary gland occurs by direct contact with the environment usually between milkings.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
explanation: Coliform (environmental) mastitis is not well controlled by standard contagious-pathogen control measures precisely because infection arises from environmental exposure between milkings, so both statements are true.

text: Potency of a drug is inversely proportional to:
explanation: Potency is defined by the dose required to produce a given effect — the lower the dose needed, the higher the potency, i.e., potency is inversely related to dose.

text: Which type of necrosis is noticed in abscess?
explanation: An abscess is a collection of pus formed by liquefactive necrosis of tissue.

text: Primary uterine inertia can be treated with:
explanation: Primary uterine inertia, often linked to hypocalcaemia and poor myometrial tone, is treated with a combination of oxytocin and calcium borogluconate.

text: Prolonged estrus sign in cattle is seen in:
explanation: Follicular (cystic follicle) disease causes persistently high oestrogen levels, resulting in prolonged/continuous oestrus (nymphomania).

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Uremia in dogs
(B). Canine Pemphigus
(C). Mania
(D). Pollakiuria
List II:
(I). Lower urinary tract infection
(II). Increased senso motor stimulation
(III). Autoimmune disease
(IV). Tongue tip necrosis
options: A – IV, B – III, C – II, D – I
A – III, B – II, C – I, D - IV
A – II, B – I, C – IV, D - III
A – I, B – IV, C – III, D - II
explanation: Uraemia can cause tongue-tip necrosis/ulceration; canine pemphigus is an autoimmune skin disease; mania relates to increased sensorimotor stimulation; pollakiuria is commonly associated with lower urinary tract infection.

text:
In tuberculin testing, which of the following types of reaction is shown by the animal?
(A). Active allergic reaction
(B). Cytotoxic hypersensitivity
(C). Delayed hypersensitivity
(D). Arthus reaction
(E). Auto-immune reaction
explanation: The tuberculin skin test is a classic example of a Type IV (delayed-type/cell-mediated) hypersensitivity reaction.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). 8th Cranial nerve
(B). Traumatic Reticulo Peritonitis
(C). 2nd Cranial nerve
(D). Abomasal ulcer
List II:
(I). Occult blood test
(II). Menace test
(III). Pole test
(IV). Colorie test
options: A – I, B – III, C – II, D – IV
A – II, B – III, C – IV, D - I
A – III, B – IV, C – I, D - II
A – IV, B – III, C – II, D - I
explanation: The pole test is used to elicit pain in traumatic reticuloperitonitis; the menace response tests the 2nd cranial (optic) nerve; abomasal ulcer is screened for via the faecal occult blood test; the 8th cranial nerve pairs with the remaining option by elimination.

text: A subunit vaccine of CoxAbic contains:
explanation: CoxAbic is a maternal subunit vaccine against avian coccidiosis prepared from purified gametocyte antigens of Eimeria maxima.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Contagious mastitis
(B). Summer mastitis
(C). Environmental mastitis
(D). Fungal mastitis
List II:
(I). Escherichia Coli
(II). Arcanobacterium pyogenes
(III). Staphylococcus aureus
(IV). Trichosporon spp.
options: A – III, B – II, C – I, D – IV
A – II, B – I, C – IV, D - III
A – IV, B – III, C – I, D - II
A – I, B – IV, C – II, D - III
explanation: Staphylococcus aureus causes contagious mastitis; Arcanobacterium (Trueperella) pyogenes causes summer mastitis; E. coli causes environmental mastitis; Trichosporon spp. cause fungal mastitis.

text: In Haematoxylin and Eosin staining, mucin takes the following colour:
explanation: Mucin is basophilic and stains pale blue with haematoxylin in routine H&E staining, rather than the pink (eosinophilic) colour of most cytoplasmic protein.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Haemonchosis
(B). Cestodiasis
(C). Babesiosis
(D). Coccidiosis
List II:
(I). Diminazene aceturate
(II). Amprolium
(III). Praziquantel
(IV). Fenbendazole
options: A – I, B – II, C – III, D – IV
A – II, B – III, C – IV, D - I
A – III, B – IV, C – I, D - II
A – IV, B – III, C – I, D - II
explanation: Fenbendazole treats haemonchosis (a nematode infection); praziquantel treats cestodiasis; diminazene aceturate treats babesiosis; amprolium treats coccidiosis.

text:
Match List I with List II:
List I:
(A). Congestive Heart failure
(B). Acute Heart failure
(C). Cardiac Murmur
(D). Cardiac Thrill
List II:
(I). Large size Leak
(II). Moderate size leak
(III). Severe pale mucous membrane
(IV). Exercise intolerance
options: A – IV, B – III, C – II, D – I
A – III, B – II, C – I, D – IV
A – II, B – I, C – IV, D – III
A – I, B – II, C – III, D – IV
explanation: Congestive heart failure causes exercise intolerance; acute heart failure presents with severe pallor of mucous membranes (shock); an audible murmur suggests a moderate-sized valve leak, while a palpable thrill suggests a larger leak.

text: Which one of the following is an ideal transducer for doing ultrasonographic examination of reticulum in a cow?
explanation: A lower-frequency (3.5 MHz) linear transducer provides the depth of penetration required to image the reticulum through the cranioventral abdominal wall of a cow.

text: Ketamine hydrochloride is under the category of:
explanation: Ketamine is classified as a dissociative anaesthetic, producing a cataleptic, analgesic state distinct from classical general anaesthesia.

text: The maximum dose rate of lignocaine hydrochloride in goat should not exceed:
explanation: The maximum recommended safe dose of lignocaine in goats is around 10 mg/kg body weight, beyond which systemic toxicity risk rises significantly.
